text: Because Wi-Fi coverage is smaller typically than the cellular one, right? So if we have users that move fast, they will move from one Wi-Fi access point to another continuously because the coverage of access points is small. So if the users travel fast, they will move from one access point to another continuously. Instead, the cellular base stations provide larger coverage. So this means that even if the user is fast, he will stay under the coverage of the same base station for a longer time. So we don't have to change base station continuously, right? That helps a lot. So using cellular, our user even if it's a fast user can remain connected with the same base station for a longer time than if that user used Wi-Fi. So that's the first advantage for cellular to support mobile users. The second reason why cellular is more suitable for mobile users is due to the technology itself. In cellular, we have specific procedures to handle.
